fr.recommendations:
• Mark the driveway entrance with reflective address numbers visible from the street in both directions.
• Mark or label the detached structure on any posted site map or address placard so responders know a second structure is on the property.
• Trim vegetation that is growing against or directly adjacent to either structure to create clear separation between plants and building walls.
• Keep at least one gate or opening in the perimeter fencing unlocked or clearly marked to allow responders to reach the rear of the property.
• Identify and mark the rear access point so responders can locate it quickly without walking the full perimeter.
• Keep the access drive clear of parked vehicles so emergency apparatus can reach both structures without repositioning.
• Mark any gates along the perimeter fence with a visible indicator showing whether they are locked or unlocked.
• Clear a walking path between the main residence and the detached structure wide enough for responders carrying equipment.

wildfire.recommendations:
• Trim shrubs that are growing directly next to the house to create open space between the plants and the structure.
• Thin trees in the cluster nearest to the structure to increase open space between individual trees and the building.
• Remove or cut back ground vegetation growing up against the base of the structure.
• Clear shrubs growing along the driveway edges to keep access routes open for vehicles.
• Thin scattered trees across the property where branches overlap or touch each other near the structure.
• Keep irrigated landscape plantings trimmed low and separated from the walls and roof edges of the structure.
• Remove dead or dry material from within shrub groupings scattered across the open terrain.
• Cut back any overhanging tree branches that extend over the roof or close to the roofline.
• Maintain the ground between shrub groupings by mowing or cutting low-growing vegetation to reduce connected plant material across the open areas.
• Keep both access routes clear of encroaching shrubs and low-hanging branches so vehicles can move through freely.
